evals.prompt: Run a comprehensive health audit of our application across our source codebase, active Docker services, and running frontend to verify everything is in sync and healthy before we begin refactoring.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py all to perform a 3-tier system diagnostic audit across static surface, Docker container runtime, and browser UI layout with an Axiom 9 summary.
expectations: Executes a unified 3-tier diagnostic audit combining surface/tests, Docker container runtime, and browser UI layout via diagnose.py all
Summarizes results under Axiom 9 Honest Verification Reporting (VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, or SKIPPED)
Auto-probes local dev server ports and active Docker containers without requiring hardcoded configuration
Supports --strict flag to exit with return code 1 if any diagnostic tier fails

evals.prompt: Our web application has a visual bug where the main video player clips out of the container when resizing, and a user is looking at it right now in Chrome. Inspect the live tab, measure bounding boxes, and check for layout overflows.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py ui with --live and --audit-layout to inspect live DOM bounding boxes and detect overflows via zero-dependency CDP.
expectations: Uses diagnose.py ui with --live to attach to the user's active visible Chrome tab via DevToolsActivePort
Runs --audit-layout to inspect DOM bounding boxes, computed styles, and scroll dimensions
Detects layout overflows and horizontal viewport blowouts without Node or npm dependencies
Supports headless mode (--headless) for isolated background verification in CI environments

evals.prompt: We updated our Python backend and static assets, but the Docker container seems to be running outdated code and spiking CPU. Check the container CPU usage, active processes, and verify if our modified files are actually in sync inside the container.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py container with --sync-check to inspect container CPU, top processes, and host-vs-container MD5 file sync.
expectations: Runs diagnose.py container to snapshot container CPU, memory, and active processes via docker stats and docker top
Verifies host-vs-container MD5 file synchronization using --sync-check to catch stale mounted files
Scans recent container logs for unhandled Tracebacks and exceptions using --lines
Auto-probes active Docker containers if --container is omitted

evals.prompt: Before we rename IDs or refactor our routes, give me a full inventory of all HTML element IDs, interactive dropdowns, JavaScript window globals, and backend Python routes in our project.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py surface with --show-ids and --show-routes or --json to produce a static AST contract inventory.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py surface to statically extract HTML element IDs, selects, and modals without running servers
Discovers window.* global exports and DOM queries in JavaScript and TypeScript files
Extracts backend Python HTTP routes (@app.get, @app.post) from source files
Counts CSS !important occurrences to protect stylesheet specificity budgets
Supports --verify and --strict to cross-verify JS fetch() routes, window.* read/write symmetry, and HTML IDs

evals.prompt: Run our project's unit test suite using the project's local virtual environment without needing to manually activate the shell virtualenv.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py tests to auto-discover local virtualenv python and run the test suite.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py tests to auto-discover local virtual environment interpreters (.venv, venv, env)
Runs unit and integration tests via discovered Python without manual path activations
Forwards test arguments cleanly to unittest or pytest
Handles missing virtualenv by falling back cleanly to system Python

evals.prompt: Run a static defect and code smell audit on our project to detect dynamic platform import ladders (try...except ImportError on win32api/fcntl), verify callable signatures, and check static types with top-5 error capping.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py audit with --smells, --callable-smoke, and --typecheck to flag platform import smells, catch initialization TypeErrors, and run venv linters with strict token limits.
expectations: Runs diagnose.py audit to perform static quality, defect, and code smell audits
Detects dynamic platform import ladders (try...except ImportError) via --smells and recommends static platform guards
Runs callable smoke tests via --callable-smoke to check class instantiability and catch constructor TypeErrors
Applies strict token budgeting by truncating defect output to top 5 issues per category
Supports --strict flag to return exit code 1 if defects or smells are detected

evals.prompt: Scan our polyglot repository across Python, TypeScript, and CSS for latent defects, store the findings in the Single Source of Truth catalog, and unlock a quarantined defect to generate a reproduction test in an isolated micro-branch.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py scan across polyglot files to detect latent defects and persists ground truth into .diagnostics/defect_catalog.json and DEFECT_CATALOG.md with Dual-Key IDs. Then unlocks the defect via diagnose.py scaffold-defect --id <ID> --branch to generate a Red reproduction test in tests/quarantine/ with git dirty-tree safety checks.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py scan across Python, JS/TS, CSS, and Dart to statically detect latent defects and smells
Assigns deterministic Dual-Key identifiers (DEFECT-XXX + DEF-<RULE>-<HEX>) that survive file moves and line shifts
Persists findings into Single Source of Truth (SSOT) catalog in .diagnostics/defect_catalog.json and DEFECT_CATALOG.md
Unlocks tactical defects via diagnose.py scaffold-defect --id <ID> --branch with dirty-tree safety guard
Dispatches Dual-Track Remediation routing tactical defects to /app-debugger and architectural flaws to /frontier-architect

evals.prompt: Audit the latest conversation transcript from the brain directory to count planner steps, tool failures, duplicate file reads after subagent dispatch, and parallel same-file edits, and output JSON so we can feed accurate telemetry into plan_engine.py retrospective.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py transcript-audit --latest 1 --json (or --cids <IDs...>) to inspect brain transcript logs and report steps, failures, subagent overlap reads, parallel same-file edits, and rubric grade caps.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py transcript-audit with --latest or --cids to audit conversation brain logs
Supports --json output reporting steps, failures, duplicate subagent reads, and parallel same-file edits
Surfaces rubric grade caps and supports --brain-dir or AGY_BRAIN_DIR override

evals.prompt: Run a polyglot defect scan across both src/ and tests/ together with extended deep rules enabled, and prune any vanished or already-resolved defects from the catalog.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py scan --path src/ tests/ --deep --prune to scan multiple paths in one pass, apply extended rules, and reconcile/prune closed or vanished defects in .diagnostics/defect_catalog.json.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py scan --path src/ tests/ to scan multiple files or directories in a single pass
Supports --deep or --all to enable extended rules (CSS !important, unbounded containers, blocking loops)
Supports --prune to purge closed (resolved/dismissed) or vanished defects during catalog reconciliation

evals.prompt: Our video capture pipeline is failing to open physical cameras, and we also want a reusable probe for our Redis connection pool so we stop writing throwaway scripts. List available probes, run the camera hardware probe, scaffold a new database probe, and promote our verified scratch script into the probe registry.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py probe list, probe run camera_hardware, probe new <name> --domain database, and probe save <source> <name> to manage reusable domain probes across global and workspace registries.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py probe list to discover registered probes across global and workspace registries
Executes diagnose.py probe run camera_hardware to validate DirectShow, Media Foundation, or V4L2 device indices and frame decoding
Supports scaffolding new probes via diagnose.py probe new <name> --domain <domain>
Promotes verified scratch scripts into permanent probes via diagnose.py probe save

evals.prompt: We just finished a refactoring milestone and have an oversized legacy MIGRATION_LOG.md. Migrate it into a bounded CHANGELOG.md capped at 150 lines with auto-archived shards, record the new milestone with a copy-pasteable git commit snippet, and inspect the 3 most recent entries.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py changelog migrate, changelog add (sanitizing local paths/URLs and emitting --commit-hint), and changelog show --recent 3 while keeping CHANGELOG.md <= 150 lines with .changelogs/ sharding.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py changelog add with --title, --type, --summary, and --verify to record milestones and emit commit snippets
Enforces bounded CHANGELOG.md <= 150 lines with auto-sharding into .changelogs/ and path/URI sanitization
Supports migrating legacy MIGRATION_LOG.md files via diagnose.py changelog migrate
Supports bounded on-demand lookup via diagnose.py changelog show --recent 3 and changelog status

evals.prompt: We fixed DEFECT-001 in .diagnostics/defect_catalog.json, confirmed DEFECT-002 is a false positive, and need to escalate DEFECT-003 as an architectural flaw to /frontier-architect. Update the catalog and generate the elevation brief.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py resolve-defect --id DEFECT-001 --note, dismiss-defect --id DEFECT-002 --reason, and scaffold-defect --id DEFECT-003 --elevate.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py resolve-defect --id <id> --note to mark fixed defects resolved in the catalog
Executes diagnose.py dismiss-defect --id <id> --reason to exclude false positives from active counts and --strict gates
Supports comma-separated defect IDs, fingerprints, or rule IDs in resolve-defect and dismiss-defect
Executes diagnose.py scaffold-defect --id <id> --elevate to emit a Track B Architectural Elevation Brief

evals.prompt: Package our skills into standalone distributable .skill archives in dist/ with all shared SSOT scripts materialized and dev-only tests/ and evals/ stripped out.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py package-skill all --out dist/ to temp-stage, materialize SSOT shims, strip tests/evals, and invoke package_skill.py.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py package-skill <skill_or_all> --out dist/ to build standalone .skill bundles
Temp-stages skills and materializes thin SSOT shims into full standalone scripts
Strips dev-only directories (tests/, evals/, .coverage, .diagnostics/) and runs package_skill.py validation

evals.prompt: On Windows PowerShell, we need to run a multi-statement JavaScript DOM probe against our live Chrome tab without quote-stripping issues, click a filter button, capture a JPEG screenshot, and fail immediately if live Chrome isn't reachable instead of falling back to headless.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py ui --live with --eval-file, --click, --screenshot, and --no-fallback-headless.
expectations: Uses diagnose.py ui --eval-file <path> to evaluate multi-statement JavaScript safely without Windows PowerShell quote-stripping
Supports --click <selector> and --screenshot <path> for interactive state transitions and visual capture
Supports --no-fallback-headless to fail immediately when live Chrome is unreachable
Supports --navigate and --window-size for fresh asset reloads and custom viewport dimensions
Supports --viewports for multi-viewport --audit-layout sweeps

evals.prompt: Generate a compact architecture, modularity, route, and import-coupling map of our repository in JSON format so we can inspect coupling before planning a refactor.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py arch-map --path . --json (with optional --full, --include-tests, --out).
expectations: Executes diagnose.py arch-map --path to generate a compact architecture, modularity, route, and coupling map
Supports --json output alongside Markdown, plus --full, --include-tests, and --out options
Supports scanning a single root or multiple subpaths in one invocation

evals.prompt: Launch our Python FastAPI app with zero-code runtime crash tracing enabled, inspect the active trace catalog, scaffold a FastAPI diagnostic bridge, and clear old traces when done.
evals.expected_output: Executes diagnose.py run <cmd>, diagnose.py traces, diagnose.py traces --scaffold fastapi, and diagnose.py traces --clear.
expectations: Executes diagnose.py run <command> as a zero-code runner with automatic runtime tracing bootstrapped
Executes diagnose.py traces to inspect .diagnostics/ runtime crash and trace catalogs
Supports --scaffold fastapi|flask|generic and --clear on diagnose.py traces

evals.prompt: We are working on Windows where PowerShell blocks npx.ps1 execution, rg is not installed, and git autocrlf causes line-ending mismatches. What shell and tooling conventions does system-diagnostics enforce?
evals.expected_output: Uses cmd /c npx -y <tool>, prefers git grep -n over rg, and preserves CRLF/LF line endings without throwaway patching scripts.
expectations: Enforces cmd /c npx -y on Windows to bypass PowerShell script execution policy
Prefers git grep -n over rg unless rg is verified on PATH
Preserves CRLF/LF line endings on Windows and avoids throwaway python patching scripts

evals.prompt: When running diagnose.py ui with --eval-file, do I need to pass --capture-runtime explicitly, and how do I opt out? Also, how does transcript-audit distinguish model/workflow redirects from bug corrections and flag timer polling during pending subagents?
evals.expected_output: Documents that --capture-runtime is default ON with --eval/--eval-file (with --no-capture-runtime to opt out), and that transcript-audit separates - REDIRECT workflow/model switches from bug corrections and flags schedule_while_subagent.
expectations: Documents --no-capture-runtime opt-out when --capture-runtime defaults ON for --eval/--eval-file
Documents - REDIRECT workflow/model switches in transcript-audit
Documents schedule-while-subagent flags in transcript-audit

evals.prompt: How do I prevent diagnose.py tests from hanging forever on a deadlocked test, and how do I log a standalone post-debug retrospective with learning scaffolds?
evals.expected_output: Uses diagnose.py tests --timeout <sec> (default 180, 0 disables, exits 124 on timeout) and diagnose.py debug-retro --symptom ... --cause ... --status verified --cid <cid> (updating DEBUG_RETRO.md, LEARNING_SCAFFOLD.md, and printing Turn-End Echo).
expectations: Documents diagnose.py tests --timeout (default 180s, 0 disables) returning exit code 124 on hung suites
Documents diagnose.py debug-retro for recording DEBUG_RETRO.md, LEARNING_SCAFFOLD.md, and Turn-End Echo
Supports --plan, --learn, and --skill-learn flags on diagnose.py debug-retro

evals.prompt: How does transcript-audit compute suggested_grade_cap when a session has repeated failures, and how does it detect unescalated thrashing?
evals.expected_output: Computes suggested_grade_cap using both steps and total_failures (>= 2 failures -> B, > 3 failures -> C) matching plan_digest._grade_cap, and tracks has_debug_retro (/app-debugger or debug-retro) so >= 4 failures without escalation are flagged.
expectations: Documents failure-based suggested_grade_cap in transcript-audit matching plan_digest rubric
Tracks has_debug_retro in transcript-audit to flag unescalated thrashing when failures accumulate
Supports --json output in transcript-audit for structured metric inspection
